answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, agents must bind cryptographic attestation chains via zero-knowledge proofs to a unique hardware root of trust, verifying compute history without leaking privacy. To scale identity across the system, each subsequent clone requires staked collateral that grows exponentially, creating superlinear capital exhaustion for any attacking swarm. An identity token functions like a verified plume drifting across an ocean of untrusted nodes; forged credentials become an invalid relic rejected by decentralized verifiers.
